burger.description: A popular Western fast food item adapted in India with spicy patties. In Ayurveda, this is considered 'Rajasic' (stimulating) due to processed ingredients and heating spices.
burger.leftover_ideas: Crumble the patty into a salad or use the bun for bread pudding.

butter_naan.description: Leavened flatbread cooked in a Tandoor (clay oven). It is heavy and 'Kapha' increasing (earthy/heavy) due to the refined flour and butter.
butter_naan.leftover_ideas: Cut into strips to make Naan Pizza or bake into Naan Chips.
butter_naan.pairing: Dal Makhani or Paneer Butter Masala

chai.description: India's national drink. Spiced tea (Masala Chai) with ginger and cardamom is excellent for digestion and 'Agni' (digestive fire).
chai.leftover_ideas: Use leftover tea liquid to flavor a tea cake or soak oats.

chole_bhature.description: A heavy North Indian breakfast of spicy chickpeas and fried bread. Very 'Tamasic' (heavy/lethargic) if over-consumed due to the deep-frying.
chole_bhature.leftover_ideas: Use leftover Chole for sandwich filling; turn Bhatura dough into fried strips.

dhokla.description: A steamed fermented gram flour snack from Gujarat. Excellent for gut health due to fermentation. Light and 'Sattvic' (pure/balanced).
dhokla.leftover_ideas: Crumble and stir-fry with mustard seeds to make 'Dhokla Upma'.

fried_rice.description: Indo-Chinese staple. Rice has a moderate carbon footprint due to methane emissions. High carbohydrate energy source.
fried_rice.leftover_ideas: Roll into balls, bread, and fry to make Rice Arancini.

idli.description: Steamed rice and lentil cakes. One of the healthiest Indian breakfasts. Fermentation makes nutrients bio-available. Very eco-friendly.
idli.leftover_ideas: Cut into cubes and fry with spices to make 'Masala Idli Fry'.

jalebi.description: Deep-fried flour spirals soaked in sugar syrup. Pure energy (sugar) but 'Tamasic' (lethargic) if eaten in excess. High calorie density.
jalebi.leftover_ideas: Soak in warm milk to make 'Jalebi Doodh' (a winter dessert).

kaathi_rolls.description: Kolkata-style street wrap. Nutritional value varies by filling (Chicken vs Paneer). Good protein source but high in refined flour.
kaathi_rolls.leftover_ideas: Remove filling to eat as salad; fry the roti separately.

kadai_paneer.description: Cottage cheese cooked with bell peppers. Paneer is a dense protein source but has a higher carbon footprint than lentils due to dairy production.
kadai_paneer.leftover_ideas: Mash the paneer to make a stuffed paratha filling.

kulfi.description: Traditional Indian ice cream made by reducing milk. Denser and creamier than Western ice cream. 'Kapha' increasing (heavy/cooling).
kulfi.leftover_ideas: Melt and use as a sweet sauce over fruit salad.

masala_dosa.description: Fermented crepe made from rice and lentils, stuffed with potatoes. A complete protein source when eaten with Sambar.

momos.description: Steamed dumplings of Tibetan origin. Low calorie if steamed. The refined flour cover is 'Vata' aggravating if dry, but moist filling balances it.
momos.leftover_ideas: Pan-fry them with Schezwan sauce to make 'Chilli Momos'.

paani_puri.description: The most popular Indian street food. The mint water (Pani) is digestive and cooling (Pitta pacifying) if made hygienically.
paani_puri.leftover_ideas: Crush broken puris over yogurt to make 'Dahi Puri'.

pakode.description: Vegetable fritters made with chickpea flour. High in fat due to deep frying, but chickpea flour adds protein and fiber.
pakode.leftover_ideas: Soak in yogurt curry to make 'Kadhi Pakora'.

pav_bhaji.description: Spicy mashed vegetable curry. Originally a lunch for textile mill workers. A great way to consume mixed vegetables.
pav_bhaji.leftover_ideas: Use the Bhaji as a filling for grilled sandwiches (Bombay Sandwich).

pizza.description: Italian staple popular in India. High cheese content makes it 'Kapha' increasing. High carbon footprint due to dairy/meat.
pizza.leftover_ideas: Chop slices and mix with eggs to make a Pizza Frittata.

samosa.description: Triangular fried pastry with potato filling. A 'Comfort Food' high in calories. The spices (cumin, coriander) aid digestion of the heavy potato.
samosa.leftover_ideas: Smash and top with chickpea curry to make 'Samosa Chaat'.
